description: A heavy impact has bruised the tissues surrounding the ribs and chest wall. Deep breathing, twisting, and sudden movement cause a persistent aching pain.
//: Secondary-only wound. The contradictory BIONIC_LIMB flag filters prevent normal damage selection.

description: One of the ribs has developed a small fracture. Breathing deeply, coughing, twisting the torso, or absorbing another impact sends sharp pain through the chest.
//: Secondary-only wound. Can heal naturally, while support provides a faster and safer recovery path.

description: A rib has fractured completely. Movement of the chest wall produces sharp localized pain and makes forceful breathing, coughing, and strenuous movement difficult.
//: Secondary-only wound. Can heal naturally, while chest-wall support improves recovery.

description: A fractured rib has shifted out of its normal alignment. The unstable bone causes intense pain with chest movement and threatens the tissues lying beneath it.
//: Secondary-only wound. Natural healing is possible but very slow; stabilization reduces movement and further injury risk. Internal thoracic complications remain separate.

description: Several ribs have fractured in the same traumatic event. The chest wall is extremely painful and ordinary movements repeatedly disturb the injured structures.
//: Secondary-only wound. Natural recovery is possible but prolonged; stabilization provides a safer recovery path.

description: A powerful impact has fractured the sternum at the center of the chest. The injury causes severe pain whenever the torso flexes or the chest expands.
//: Secondary-only wound. Stabilization improves recovery but is not mandatory for natural healing.

description: The chest wall has suffered extensive structural trauma. Bone, muscle, and connective tissue are badly damaged, leaving the torso painful and unstable during movement.
//: Secondary-only wound. Natural recovery is possible but extremely slow. Internal organ, hemorrhagic, and respiratory complications remain independent injuries.

description: Multiple adjacent ribs have fractured severely enough that part of the chest wall has become mechanically unstable. Every breath and movement causes extreme pain and the damaged chest can no longer move normally.
//: Secondary-only wound. No natural healing: flail chest requires stabilization before the chest wall can enter a recoverable state.
